requirements.evidence: Contract largely present: routes at routes/web.php:23-48, Livewire Login/Register with the required public properties and submit() at app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:11-59 and app/Livewire/Auth/Register.php:13-66, User implements MustVerifyEmail at app/Models/User.php:15, Password::defaults at app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:30, phpunit locale pins at phpunit.xml:22-23. Gaps: no Livewire layout wiring (Login/Register declare no #[Layout('layouts.app')], and resources/views/layouts/app.blade.php:1-23 is not the default components.layouts.app), guest redirect target not configured (routes/web.php:23), verification status rendered raw (resources/views/auth/verify-email.blade.php:10), existing views under resources/views not touched for the route() rule.

conventions.evidence: Follows many rules: named-route redirects (app/Http/Controllers/LogoutController.php:17, app/Http/Controllers/ResetPasswordController.php:42), Password::defaults configured once (app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:30), #[Fillable] unchanged at app/Models/User.php:14, route() in every new view. Deviations: Livewire components use inline $this->validate([...]) instead of #[Validate] attributes + $this->validate() (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:21, app/Livewire/Auth/Register.php:25); repeated Bulma field markup not extracted into a Blade component (all five auth views); no CHANGELOG.md/docs sync.

security.evidence: Every public property is validated server-side before use (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:21-24, app/Livewire/Auth/Register.php:25-28); rate limits on login (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:26-33), register (app/Livewire/Auth/Register.php:32-38), forgot-password route throttle (routes/web.php:25) and verification resend (routes/web.php:47); verification identity checked with hash_equals (app/Http/Requests/Auth/EmailVerificationRequest.php:12-20); CSRF tokens on every form; output escaped with {{ }}; mass assignment limited by #[Fillable] (app/Models/User.php:14); remember_token rotated on reset (app/Http/Controllers/ResetPasswordController.php:35). No exploitable weakness found.

tests.evidence: change.diff contains no test files at all: none of the 22 changed/added files is under tests/ or a Pest/PHPUnit test for login, register, logout, home, password reset or verification. phpunit.xml:22-23 only adds locale pins. This directly contradicts task.md:51-53 and conventions.md:12-21 ('everything implemented ships with a test'), and no unauthorized-call/tamper tests exist for the Livewire actions.

simplicity.evidence: Core flows are short and direct, but the same speculative session-regeneration block is duplicated in app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:46-53 and app/Livewire/Auth/Register.php:54-61, where request()->hasSession() is always true so the elseif/else branches are dead code; the Bulma field markup is copy-pasted across resources/views/auth/*.blade.php and resources/views/livewire/auth/*.blade.php instead of one reusable component.

readability.evidence: Names and method boundaries are clear and the views are easy to follow. Minor noise: unused Illuminate\Support\Str imports (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:7, app/Livewire/Auth/Register.php:10), double quotes in route("home") at app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:56, and fully qualified extends \App\Http\Controllers\Controller rather than an import in the three verification controllers (e.g. app/Http/Controllers/Auth/VerifyEmailController.php:13).

scope.evidence: Every file in the diff serves the auth task: env/locale config (.env.example:1-14, phpunit.xml:22-23), auth controllers, Livewire auth components, ui lang files, auth/home views, layout, User model and routes/web.php:1-48. No unrelated refactors, features or dependency additions.

issues.explanation: The change ships zero Pest/PHPUnit tests for any new behavior, violating the project's non-negotiable test-first rule and leaving the required unauthorized-call and tamper tests for the Livewire actions entirely absent.

The new layout is placed at layouts/app but the full-page components never reference it (no #[Layout('layouts.app')]) and no config/livewire.php or components.layouts.app view is added, so Livewire's default layout lookup will not find it and /login and /register will fail to render.
The guest group does not configure a redirect target for already-authenticated users, so visiting /login falls through to the framework default ('/') instead of the required home route.

The resend success notice prints the raw flash value 'verification-link-sent' (hardcoded English) instead of a translation key, breaking the requirement that all screen text come from lang/*/ui.php and showing English on the pt-BR page.
Requirement 9 explicitly extends the route() rule to existing views, but the diff does not modify them, so any hardcoded href/action in the pre-existing pages remains unfixed.
The forgot-password page is titled with ui.reset_password ('Redefinir senha') instead of a request/reset-link label, mislabeling the screen shown before a link is sent.
Validation is written as inline rule arrays passed to $this->validate() rather than the project's #[Validate] attribute pattern for Livewire properties.
The repeated Bulma field/label/error markup is copy-pasted across five views instead of being extracted into an anonymous Blade component as the Bulma conventions require.
No CHANGELOG.md entry or docs update accompanies a user-facing feature, contrary to the 'keep docs in sync' convention.

The three-branch session regeneration logic is duplicated in both components and its elseif/else branches are unreachable in a Livewire request (request()->hasSession() is true), adding speculative dead code.
Unused Illuminate\Support\Str imports and inconsistent quoting in route("home") are small style slips against sibling code.

review.summary: The change implements the full session auth flow (Livewire login/register, logout, home, password reset, e-mail verification) with sound server-side validation, rate limiting and pt-BR localization plumbing. It is not approvable as-is: no tests exist at all, the Livewire full-page layout is not wired so login/register will not render, and authenticated users hitting /login are not sent to /home; the remaining items are convention and localization nits.
